clue.text: Perhaps Ida's style of dress

blocks.note: first meaning: Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta is ... Ida, so Ida is an example of a royal daughter
second meaning: a close-fitting dress cut in panels without a waist seam

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Ida as one example of the title; Princess Ida is the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera. The 's is just a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: A king's daughter is a royal title holder, and a princess line is a fitted dress cut without a waist seam.

clue.text: Tomboy in a part acting with alacrity

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: pt is the abbreviation for part
a romp is an old word for a boisterous girl, a tomboy

explanation.surface: A tomboy cast in a play role acts quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romp' as a tomboy is a dated sense. 'Acting' plays on the theatre, but here it simply means behaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt means done without delay, so someone acting with alacrity is being quick and ready.

clue.text: Indoors and out, almost lost without smell

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
letters that are lost have wandered from their places and need finding in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word out without its last letter

explanation.surface: Inside and outside, nearly everything is lost and nothing has any scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour is smell, and the in- prefix negates it, so the word describes something scentless.

clue.text: Mild pope

blocks.note: first meaning: gentle, merciful, of weather or temperament
second meaning: the name taken by fourteen popes

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a gentle pontiff; in fact it is two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means lenient or temperate, and it is also the papal name used by several pontiffs.

clue.text: Bismuth has upset the gentleman

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset tips the letters over so they read from the bottom up

blocks.note: Bi is the chemical symbol for bismuth
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemical element has unsettled a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: In colonial India, sahib was the respectful title for a European man, equivalent to sir or master.

clue.text: Note carried by island's messenger

indicators.note: something carried by another is held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Herm is one of the Channel Islands, plus the S of the possessive
a musical note

explanation.surface: A note carried by courier from a small island.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside HERM'S, just before the S. Herm is a tiny car-free island in the Channel Islands, off France.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this winged-sandalled god carried the gods' messages, so he is their herald.

clue.text: Part of the car to wear out

blocks.note: first meaning: the pipe carrying waste gases from the engine
second meaning: to tire completely

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a worn car component; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The tailpipe system expels engine fumes, and as a verb the word means to tire or use up completely.

clue.text: The policeman's code

blocks.note: first meaning: Inspector ..., Colin Dexter's Oxford detective
second meaning: the dot-and-dash telegraph alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a police code of conduct; it is the TV detective's surname and Samuel Morse's signalling code.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Morse is a famous fictional detective, and the dot-dash telegraphic alphabet bears the same surname.

clue.text: A bloomer — 15 was mistaken

indicators.note: something mistaken has gone wrong, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: the answer to 15 across
taken as written

explanation.surface: A blunder: the tent was in the wrong place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake, matching 'was mistaken', but it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: This scented climbing annual flowers freely, so it is a bloomer in the gardener's sense.

clue.text: He's not a believer in coasting when going downhill

indicators.note: going downhill means deteriorating, so the word's letters fall into disorder

blocks.note: all eight letters

explanation.surface: A sceptic will not trust freewheeling down a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person holds that God's existence cannot be known, so they neither believe nor deny.

clue.text: Heigh-ho! No senors could be so arrogant

indicators.note: 'could be' says these letters might turn into something else once rearranged

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of the exclamation and the Spanish gentlemen

explanation.surface: A sigh that no Spanish gentleman could carry himself with such arrogance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rides a tall mount looks down on others, so the idiom means haughty and superior.

clue.text: Saw gypsy gone into the lead

indicators.note: what has gone into something else ends up enclosed by it

blocks.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a rover is a wanderer, as a gypsy traditionally is

explanation.surface: Someone saw a traveller head into the front of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The lead' looks like being in front; it is the metal, symbol Pb, which wraps round ROVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same thing as a familiar wise adage.

clue.text: Rolling round, turned up fast

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so its letters read backwards

blocks.note: a round shape is the letter O
taken as written, then turned
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Something rolling round turned up quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling' looks like movement, but it is the slang sense of rolling in money.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rolling, or rolling in it, is informal for being very rich, which is what wealthy and lavish means.

clue.text: Left artist to it, resulting in a picture

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
RA is a Royal Academician
'to' attaches the word it to what precedes

explanation.surface: Leaving the painter to get on with it, and a picture is the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted likeness of a sitter is one kind of picture, so the word fits as an example.

clue.text: Desertion from a military establishment not initially simple

indicators.note: not initially means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
an army post is a military station
easy, without its first letter

explanation.surface: Going AWOL from a garrison is far from simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning one's religion or party is a defection, so the word means deserting a belief.

clue.text: Toledo's first blade, finds a home in America

indicators.note: first says take only the opening letter of the city's name

blocks.note: the opening letter of the Spanish city
an épée is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: Toledo's finest sword ends up housed across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: Toledo was famous for its sword-making, which is why a blade follows it in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A conical tent of skins was the dwelling of Plains peoples of North America, so it is an American home.

clue.text: Yokels left out of joke

indicators.note: what is out of a word has been taken away from it

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
a pleasantry is a jocular remark

explanation.surface: Country bumpkins left out of a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Yokels are rustic country folk, and the collective noun means the rural labouring class.

clue.text: Child permitted to be understood

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child
licit means lawful, allowed

explanation.surface: A child allowed to be understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implied but not stated outright is tacitly assumed, which is the sense of understood here.

clue.text: Notes and letter from abroad exactly copying the original

blocks.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sic is printed to show a quotation is copied exactly as written

explanation.surface: A note and a foreign letter transcribed word for word from the source.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequence of musical tones played or written down makes up a piece, so notes collectively are the art itself.

clue.text: The first state finishes

blocks.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
ends are finishes

explanation.surface: The first state completes the task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first state' reads as one phrase, perhaps Delaware; the definition is only 'The first'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the calends was day one of each month, so it names the first.

clue.text: Green with love for a Scot

indicators.note: 'with X for Y' means X takes Y's place in the word

blocks.note: Arcadian means rustic and pastoral, of the green countryside
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
the letter that gets replaced

explanation.surface: A Scotsman turns green with love.
explanation.walkthrough: The first A of ARCADIAN becomes O. 'Green with love' reads as jealousy or lovesickness, but green is the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: An Orcadian comes from Orkney, the islands off northern Scotland, so this islander is a Scot.

clue.text: File is well hidden during revolutionary uprising

indicators.note: hidden during says these words are tucked inside another
in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
taken as written
well and so are both sentence fillers

explanation.surface: A secret file stays well hidden through a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary uprising' reads as one phrase, a revolt; split it, and the adjective is a communist while 'uprising' turns the down answer over.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a collection of papers on a person or subject, the same thing as a case file.

clue.text: Notes taken into examination, a stiff test

indicators.note: what is taken into something ends up inside it

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken examination
two musical notes

explanation.surface: Taking notes into an exam is a severe trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically trial by ordeal tested guilt through pain, so the word means any harrowing trial.

clue.text: Tract gladly (they used to say) rented out

indicators.note: 'say' points to the spoken word, and 'used to' marks it as an old-fashioned word

blocks.note: lief is an archaic word for gladly, as in 'I'd as lief'
a let house is one rented out

explanation.surface: A pamphlet once happily rented out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short printed pamphlet, usually religious or political, handed out on a single folded sheet.

clue.text: 'e's among the leaders of Arabian Muslims, exacting respect

definitions.text: 'e's among the leaders of Arabian Muslims, exacting respect

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters, so take the first of each following word
among puts one piece in the midst of others

blocks.note: the opening letters of the four words
he with the H dropped, as written

explanation.surface: He is one of the Arab world's rulers, a man who commands deference.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes between the second and third initials. Read whole, the clue describes the man: he is one of the leaders of Arab Muslims and commands respect.
explanation.definitionFit: An ameer, or emir, is a Muslim ruler or commander, a respected leader in the Arab world.

clue.text: Well I got swallowed up by the European giant

indicators.note: what is swallowed up ends up inside the one doing the swallowing

blocks.note: der is German for the
a spa is a mineral spring
taken as written

explanation.surface: Well, I was eaten by the giant from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The European' is 'the' in a European language, here German. Giant Despair is the ogre of Doubting Castle in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: In Bunyan's allegory, Giant Despair imprisons Christian and Hopeful, so the giant is named for hopelessness.

clue.text: Look for water and plunge into it

blocks.note: first meaning: to search for underground water with a divining rod
second meaning: to immerse or drench, an alternative spelling of douse

explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' seems to refer back to the water, which neatly links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A water diviner walks with a forked stick to find springs, and the same word means to dunk or soak.

clue.text: Was the alliance's dissolution completely void?

indicators.note: a dissolution breaks something up, so the letters come apart and regroup

blocks.note: all fifteen letters, including the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Asking whether a broken-up alliance's agreement was wholly null.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something spotless or entirely empty, with nothing left in it at all.

clue.text: On Thursday, a sudden migration affects a bird

blocks.note: Th is the short form of Thursday
a rush, as in a gold rush, is a sudden movement of people to one place

explanation.surface: A sudden mass movement on Thursday disturbs a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The song thrush and mistle thrush are common speckled songbirds, so the word names one kind of bird.

clue.text: Fighting disrupts trade in settlement

indicators.note: to disrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece bursts inside the other

blocks.note: to deal is to trade
a fray is a fight or brawl

explanation.surface: War disrupts commerce in a colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settlement' suggests a village, but it is the paying of a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray costs is to pay them, so the noun is the payment that settles an account.
